title: Case interview maths cheat sheet: formulas, shortcuts and a calm routine
description: Everything for case interview maths on one page: the twenty formulas, five mental maths shortcuts and a six-step routine for staying calm.
hook: This is everything you need for case maths on one page: the formulas, the shortcuts and a routine for staying calm while you work out loud. Keep it open while you practise.
body:
The formulas

ProfitRevenue − Costs
Profit marginProfit ÷ Revenue
MarkupProfit ÷ Cost
Contribution marginPrice − Variable cost per unit
Breakeven volumeFixed costs ÷ Contribution margin per unit
PaybackInvestment ÷ Annual net cash gain (extra profit or saving)
ROIAnnual profit ÷ Investment
EBITDARevenue − COGS − Operating costs (excl. depreciation & amortisation)
Expected valueΣ (outcome × probability)
PerpetuityCash flow ÷ r (growing: CF ÷ (r − g))
NPV ruleInvest if NPV > 0
CAGR(End ÷ Start)^(1/years) − 1
Market shareOur sales ÷ Market sales
Elasticity% change in volume ÷ % change in price
UtilisationActual output ÷ Maximum output
LTVProfit per customer per year × Years retained
CACSales & marketing spend ÷ New customers
ChurnCustomers lost ÷ Customers at start
Cost-to-revenueEach cost line ÷ Revenue, over time
Net working capitalInventory + Receivables − Payables

The formulas explained, with notes.

Five shortcuts

  • Big numbers: count the zeros separately
  • Percentages: build from 10% and 1%
  • Break-even: fixed costs ÷ profit per unit
  • Growth over a few years
  • The rule of 72 for doubling time

A routine for staying calm

  1. Say what you are going to calculate, and why, before you start.
  2. Write the numbers down neatly, with units.
  3. Round to friendly numbers and say that you are rounding.
  4. Talk through each step; silence makes interviewers nervous too.
  5. Check the answer is the right size.
  6. Say what the number means for the client.

For practice, try these mental maths questions and read the full case maths guide.
outro: You do not have to get all of this right at once. Pick one thing from this guide to focus on in your next practice case.
